claims.text: The proposed method integrates phase-field modeling, thermomechanical coupling, and novel interatomic potentials to guide alloy processing.
The integrated simulation-guided processing method will improve phase stability in multiphase alloys.
The integrated simulation-guided processing method will refine the microstructure of multiphase alloys.
The integrated simulation-guided processing method will optimize properties in multiphase alloys.
The initial multiphase metallic alloy has a coarse and potentially metastable microstructure.
Precisely regulated temperature, strain, and deformation rate are the relevant processing controls.
Targeted phase evolution and microstructural changes will refine grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
Advanced phase-field modeling captures coupled thermodynamic and kinetic processes.
The coupled thermodynamic and kinetic processes drive phase transformation.
The coupled thermodynamic and kinetic processes drive grain refinement.
Simultaneous phase transformation and grain refinement produce more thermodynamically stable phases.
Simultaneous phase transformation and grain refinement optimize macroscopic properties.
The proposed processing method will produce finer and more stable phases than conventional treatments.
The proposed processing method will improve mechanical, thermal, or electrical properties relative to conventional treatments.
Traditional heat treatments or mechanical processing generally address only one or two of phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization rather than all three simultaneously.
The hypothesis is applicable to multiphase alloys under carefully controlled thermomechanical conditions.
